features.name: Agent chat
features.summary: Chat with Muse, which runs a tool-using agent loop in the browser and streams replies through the server's LLM proxy.

acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Given The chat composer is focused with text entered, when The user presses Enter without Shift, then The form is submitted and the message is sent; Shift+Enter does not send..
AC2: Given A turn is in progress, when The user clicks Stop, then The request is aborted. No error banner is shown for the cancellation..

AC3: Given The model replies with tool calls, when A turn runs, then Each tool is run on the server and its result is fed back to the model. The loop continues until the model answers or 12 steps are reached..

AC4: Given The server has no OPENAI_API_KEY, when The browser calls /api/llm, then The server returns 503 with code no_api_key. The client maps it to sampling_disabled and chat is disabled with the message "The assistant isn't available on this account…"..

AC5: Given A request carries tier "default" or any other value, when The proxy builds the upstream request, then "default" maps to the Thorough model and anything else maps to the quick model. A client-sent model is ignored..
AC6: Given The provider returns HTTP 429, when A turn runs, then The assistant message shows 'Muse hit a usage limit. Wait a minute, then send again.'..

AC7: Given The chat is empty, when The Chat page renders, then A welcome screen with example prompt chips is shown. Clicking a chip fills the composer and submits it if the assistant is available and idle..
AC8: Given A tool action needs approval, when The assistant message renders, then A card with the heading, detail rows, and Allow / Don't allow buttons is shown..
AC9: Given The user asks to apply for a job and the message is not an email request, when The model is called, then mail_search and mail_send are removed from the tools offered for that turn..
AC10: Given A reply stops because of the token limit, when The turn finishes, then The message shows 'The reply was cut short. Ask for less at once.'..

document.objective: Lets a user ask Muse for something in plain words and watch it answer and act, using tools for goals, documents, connected services and the browser, with risky actions held for approval.
document.summary: Replies stream in as Muse writes them, and the user can stop a reply from any device. Turns run on the server, so a reply keeps going if the tab is closed and shows on every device; one turn runs at a time. Muse can take up to 12 steps of tool use in a turn. Fast replies in seconds; Thorough uses a stronger model. When the assistant is unavailable, the chat says so. In a job-application turn, Muse can't use email.
userStories: As a user, I want to send a message and see Muse's reply stream in, so that I get answers without waiting for the full response.
As a user, I want to stop a response in progress, so that I can cancel a turn I no longer want.
As a user, I want clear error messages when the assistant is unavailable or rate-limited, so that I know how to recover.
As a user, I want example prompts on an empty chat, so that I can see what Muse can do.
As a user, I want to see which tools Muse ran and to approve sensitive actions, so that I stay in control.

Composer: Enter to send, Shift+Enter for newline, Stop button that cancels the in-flight turn
Agent loop: streaming, tool execution, 12-step cap, truncation notice
LLM proxy: server-side key injection and tier-to-model routing
Pre-model intent shortcuts in run.js: document-step verification, job-research nudge, open application link
outOfScope: Internals of individual tools, such as Library, Goals, Ideas, Gmail and the Chrome extension
Approval workflow logic in workflow/approvals.js (not read)
Prompt content in server/agent/prompt.js and the intent regexes in server/agent/runtime.js (makeIntents) (not read in detail)
Tracing and observability backend
Settings page, memory and reset
functionalRequirements: Pressing Enter without Shift submits the composer text; Shift+Enter inserts a newline; empty text or a busy state does nothing.
While a turn runs, the Send button is hidden, the Stop button is shown, and the input and check-in button are disabled.
The agent loop repeats model calls while the model requests tools, up to 12 steps.
Tool errors and unknown tools are returned to the model as 'Error: …' tool results instead of crashing the turn.
The browser sends only a tier; the server pins the model (quick = gpt-4o-mini, default = gpt-4o unless overridden by env).
If the server has no API key, the proxy returns 503 code no_api_key and the UI shows the 'assistant isn't available' message and disables the composer.
A reply that ends at the token limit shows 'The reply was cut short. Ask for less at once.'
Pending approvals are rendered as cards with Allow and Don't allow buttons.
When the user asks to apply, the Gmail tools (mail_search, mail_send) are withheld from the model for that turn.

risks: run.js uses regex intent heuristics (affirmations, 'again', 'continue') to force deterministic paths, and these may misfire on ordinary messages.

document.howItWorks: The Chat page (features/chat/chat.js) sends the message to POST /api/agent/turn through agent/client.js and agent/run.js, and renders the streamed events. server/agent/http.js hands the request to runTurn in server/agent/runtime.js, which saves the messages as it goes (server/userdata.js, chat_messages), builds the prompt (server/agent/prompt.js) and runs the loop in server/agent/loop.js with the tools in server/agent/tools/, up to MAX_STEPS = 12. server/agent/llm.js calls OpenAI with the server-held key and a model chosen from the tier. Approvals and Chrome-bridge calls wait in agent_waits and are answered through /api/agent/answer; Stop calls /api/agent/cancel.

features.name: Approvals
features.summary: Muse stops and shows an approval card before sending mail, changing the calendar or clicking Submit; the user approves or declines.

acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Given a tool asks for approval, when the card appears, then the chat shows that Muse is waiting for the user's approval.
AC2: Given an approval card is showing, when the user clicks Approve, then the tool continues with a yes.
AC3: Given an approval card is showing, when the user clicks Decline, then the tool continues with a no.
AC4: Given an approval card is still waiting, when the turn ends, then the card resolves as no answer.
AC5: Given the user answered a card, when the tool resumes, then the outcome is written to the activity audit.

document.objective: Makes Muse stop and ask before a sensitive action: a tool pauses, an approval card appears in chat, and the action goes ahead only if the user approves.
document.summary: Before Muse does something that changes or sends anything, the chat shows a card saying what it wants to do, and Muse waits. The user approves or declines; if nobody answers before the turn ends, nothing happens. Each answer is shown on the card and written to the activity log. Cards are saved on the server, so the user can answer from any device, and a turn waits up to 4 minutes for an answer.

features.name: Goals
features.summary: Goals with a plan of steps, measurable targets and deadlines, which Muse works through and marks done only with tool evidence — including the job-search tools (find postings, score fit) and the application tracker that job-search goals use.

acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Given Muse is connected and not busy, when the user submits a goal in the Goals form, then Muse is asked to plan it with every step left as todo.
AC2: Given Muse calls create_goal, when it passes more than 8 steps or none, then at most 8 steps are kept, and a goal with no steps is refused.
AC3: Given only bookkeeping tools ran this turn, when Muse calls update_step with status done, then the tool refuses because no tool did any work this turn.
AC4: Given a web_search ran this turn, when Muse marks a step done citing a different tool, then the tool refuses and lists the tools that did run.
AC5: Given Muse calls jobs_search, when it passes neither keywords nor company boards, then the tool refuses and asks for a job title or boards.
AC6: Given the Library has no résumé, when Muse calls score_fit for a posting, then the tool refuses and asks the user to add a résumé.
AC7: Given a tracked job is drafted, when Muse marks it applied with no approved Submit click and no confirmation email this turn, then the tool refuses and points to Gmail or the Goals page.
AC8: Given Muse found the employer's email this turn, when it marks a job as interview, then the user is asked to confirm before it counts.
AC9: Given a goal exists, when Muse calls revise_plan with changed steps, then the user sees a before/after card and nothing changes unless they approve.

document.objective: Lets a user set a goal, such as getting an interview within 30 days, that Muse turns into a plan of steps and works through, marking a step done only when it actually did the work.
document.summary: The user creates a goal from the Goals page or in chat. Muse only marks a step in progress or done when a tool it ran in that turn did the work. For job searches it finds postings on employers' own hiring pages, scores the user's résumé against each one, and tracks applications against a target and deadline. Recording an interview or offer asks the user to confirm, and changing the plan needs the user's approval.
userStories: As a job seeker, I want to state a goal and get a concrete plan so that I know the next steps.
As a user, I want Muse to mark progress only when it really did the work so that the plan stays honest.
As a job seeker, I want postings found and scored against my résumé so that I apply where I fit.
As a job seeker, I want applications tracked against a target and deadline so that I can see whether I'm on pace.

features.name: Daily check-in
features.summary: A background check-in, from a button or once a day, where Muse reviews goals and connected services, acts where it can and leaves a progress brief.

acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Given the Goals page is open, when the user clicks the check-in button, then Muse runs a check-in turn.
AC2: Given "Every day" is on and a check-in already ran today, when the five-minute timer fires, then no second check-in runs that day.
AC3: Given "Every day" is on and it is before 9am, when the timer fires, then the check-in waits until 9am.
AC4: Given "Every day" is on but Muse is busy or there are no goals, when the timer fires, then no check-in runs.
AC5: Given a check-in runs, when Muse gets its instruction, then it is told the user is away and not to send emails.
AC6: Given a check-in finishes, when Muse writes its reply, then it leaves a three-line progress brief and what needs the user's decision.

document.objective: Lets Muse work on the user's goals while they're away: once a day, or from a button, it reviews goals, ideas and connected services, does what it can without the user, and leaves a short progress brief in chat.
document.summary: The check-in is an agent turn with a fixed instruction: check Gmail for application confirmations and replies, update tracked applications, work out pace against a job-search target, search for more postings when behind, never send email or submit applications, and end with a three-line brief. With "Every day" on, the open app starts it once a day from 9am when Muse is free; once started, it runs on the server and finishes even if the tab is closed.
userStories: As a job seeker, I want Muse to make progress on my goals each day without me asking, so that I don't fall behind.
As a user, I want a short brief of what changed and what needs my decision when I come back.

outOfScope: A server-side scheduler (the app must be open)
The goal and connector tools the check-in uses (their own specs)

The system runs the daily check-in at most once a day, after 9am, only when it is switched on, Muse is free, and there is at least one goal.
The system tells Muse not to send emails or submit applications during a check-in.

features.name: Ideas
features.summary: Muse captures ideas from the conversation and suggests turning them into goals.

acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Given An API client, when it POSTs /api/ideas with a blank or missing title, then the response is 400 with 'title is required'..
AC2: Given An API client, when it POSTs a valid idea, then the response is 201 with the created idea, and the title is capped at 200 characters..
AC3: Given An idea id that does not exist for the user, when the client sends PATCH or DELETE, then the response is 404 'no such idea'..
AC4: Given An unsupported HTTP method on /api/ideas, when the request is made, then the response is 405 'method not allowed'..
AC5: Given A user opens the Ideas page and has no 'new' ideas, when the page renders, then rule-based starter ideas appear under 'Starter ideas'..
AC6: Given A user with an active LLM session, when they press 'Update with Muse', then Muse creates ideas with status 'new', and the page shows them under 'New from Muse'..
AC7: Given A stored idea, when the user presses Save, then its status is set to 'saved' and it moves to the Saved group..
AC8: Given An idea card, when the user presses 'Not for me' on a stored idea, then its status becomes dismissed and the card disappears..
AC9: Given An idea card, when the user presses 'Do it', then the idea is marked done and Muse is sent a message to carry it out..
AC10: Given A chat where the user shares an idea, when Muse calls save_idea with a title already on the page, then nothing is created and the tool replies 'Already on the Ideas page.'..

document.objective: Gives the user a page of ideas, some suggested by Muse and some they saved, that they can act on, keep, turn into a goal or dismiss.
document.summary: Until Muse has learned enough to suggest ideas of its own, the page shows starter ideas. Ideas are grouped as new or starter, saved, and acted on. Each card offers Do it, Save, Make it a goal, or Not for me. In chat, Muse can save an idea the user mentions or one it suggests. Ideas are kept per user, so they follow the user across devices.
userStories: As a user, I want to see suggested ideas so that I get prompts for things I could do soon.
As a user, I want to save or dismiss ideas so that the list reflects what I care about.
As a user, I want to tell Muse to do an idea or turn it into a goal so that I can act on it quickly.
As a user, I want to say 'idea: ...' in chat so that Muse stores it on my Ideas page.

Ideas page rendering and grouping by status
Starter ideas from rules, saved to the server when acted on

outOfScope: Goal planning after 'Make it a goal' (Goals feature)
The content of rule-based starter ideas (rules.js not read)
Building the ideaContext prompt (context.js not read)
Database schema and auth internals

POST /api/ideas requires a non-empty title, truncates it to 200 characters, and returns 201 with { idea }.
PATCH /api/ideas/:id returns the updated idea, or 404 'no such idea'.
DELETE /api/ideas/:id returns { removed: id }, or 404 when the idea is missing.
Methods other than those listed return 405 on the Vercel functions.
The Ideas page hides dismissed ideas and groups the rest into New or Starter, Saved, and Acted on (done or goal).
Update with Muse asks the LLM for 4 ideas, keeps at most 6, and saves each as status 'new' with by 'muse'.
Not for me on a starter idea only records its rule key in the user’s saved settings; on a stored idea it sets status to dismissed.
save_idea skips a title that already exists, ignoring case, and otherwise stores the idea as saved.

risks: PATCH passes the body straight to updateIdea; server/ideas.js does no field validation (db.js not read).
The Not for me action on a starter idea is stored only in client state (skippedRules), so it may not persist across devices.
Failures to persist a status change (Do it, Save, dismiss) are silently swallowed by empty catch blocks, so the UI can drift from the server.
Muse-generated idea persistence also swallows errors, so some of the 4 to 6 ideas can be lost silently.
The page's Delete action is a soft dismissal (status dismissed). Whether the API ever hard-deletes from the UI is unclear.
No automated tests for Ideas were found in the files I read.
openQuestions: What rules produce starter ideas, and when does the fingerprint trigger regeneration (rules.js was not read)?
How does currentUserId identify users when there is no login?
Should dismissed ideas be permanently removed, or do they still feed the 'avoid ideas like this' behavior?
Is a QA verification pass wanted? There is no QA evidence in the repository, so a QA Engineer task to verify these criteria is recommended.
limitations: I did not read rules.js, context.js, server/db.js, db/schema.sql, core/api.js, or the tests.
The Express route wiring in server/index.js was not verified, so local server behavior is assumed to match the Vercel handlers.
Nothing was run, so all criteria are static code observations and not verified behavior.
document.howItWorks: server/ideas.js holds the handlers for GET/POST /api/ideas and PATCH/DELETE /api/ideas/:id, shared by the Vercel functions and the local Express server, scoped by user id. The Ideas page renders rule-based starters until Muse generates personalised ideas (status 'new') through the model. Chat uses the save_idea tool.

features.name: Library
features.summary: Upload documents (text extracted and stored in Postgres) that Muse searches and cites.

acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Given A signed-in user with stored documents, when The client sends GET /api/docs, then The response is 200 with { docs: [...] }..
AC2: Given A pasted-text request with title and text, when The client sends POST /api/docs, then The document is created and the response is 201 with { doc }..
AC3: Given A POST without a title, when The client sends it without a file, then The response is 400 "title is required"..
AC4: Given An uploaded file larger than 3MB, when The client sends POST /api/docs, then The response is 413 "file is too large (max 3MB)"..
AC5: Given An uploaded file that yields no text, when The client sends POST /api/docs, then The response is 422 "no readable text could be extracted from this file"..
AC6: Given An uploaded file with no title, when The client sends POST /api/docs, then The title defaults to the filename without its extension..
AC7: Given A document id that does not exist for the user, when The client sends DELETE /api/docs/:id, then The response is 404 "no such document"..
AC8: Given An unsupported HTTP method, when The client sends it to /api/docs/:id, then The response is 405..

document.objective: Lets a user keep documents, such as a résumé, pasted as text or uploaded as a file, so Muse can search and cite them.
document.summary: The user pastes text with a title or uploads a file of up to 3 MB. Only the text is kept, up to 60,000 characters; the original file isn't stored. Documents belong to the signed-in user, who can delete any of them. Muse uses them for things like scoring the résumé against a job posting.
userStories: As a user I want to paste or upload a document so that the agent can use it.
As a user I want to list my documents so that I can see what is stored.
As a user I want to delete a document so that it is no longer stored or searchable.

Create a document from an uploaded file with text extraction
outOfScope: Library UI and the agent's search, read and cite tools (not read)
Storage of the original uploaded file
Editing an existing document
Text extraction internals (server/extract.js, not read)
Database layer internals (server/db.js, not read)
functionalRequirements: GET /api/docs returns { docs } for the current user.
POST /api/docs with title and text creates a document and returns 201 with { doc }.
POST /api/docs without a title or without text returns 400.
Pasted text is truncated to 60,000 characters.
An uploaded file over 3MB is rejected with 413.
An empty uploaded file is rejected with 400.
An uploaded file with no extractable text is rejected with 422.
An uploaded file without a title uses its filename without the extension as the title.
DELETE /api/docs/:id returns the removed title, or 404 if the document does not exist.
Methods other than GET and POST on /api/docs, and other than DELETE on /api/docs/:id, return 405.

risks: Only extracted text is stored, so a file whose text cannot be extracted is lost and the original cannot be recovered.
Text from pasted documents is silently truncated at 60,000 characters, and nothing tells the user.

openQuestions: Should users be told when pasted text is truncated?
How does currentUserId identify users, and is there real authentication?

document.howItWorks: The API is GET/POST /api/docs and DELETE /api/docs/:id, as Vercel Node functions sharing handlers in server/docs.js with the local Express server. Uploads arrive base64-encoded and server/extract.js pulls out the text, which is stored in Postgres per user id.

features.name: Connectors
features.summary: Gmail, Google Calendar and Contacts connectors (Google OAuth, or sample data) that give Muse mail, calendar and contact tools.

acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Given A connector is not connected, when The user clicks Continue with Google in the consent panel, then The browser navigates to /api/google/authorize..
AC2: Given The Gmail connector is connected, when The user views its permission controls, then The Allow button is disabled with the note that sending email always needs approval..
AC3: Given The Google status endpoint reports connected, when initConnectors runs at boot or after the redirect, then Both Gmail and Calendar are marked on together..
AC4: Given Google is connected, when The user clicks Disconnect Google, then Gmail and Calendar are turned off and the disconnect is audited..
AC5: Given Gmail is connected and Muse calls mail_send, when The tool runs, then An approval card asks the user to allow the send, and the message is sent only after approval..
AC6: Given Calendar permission is Ask me first, when Muse calls calendar_add, then An approval card shows the event and time before the event is added..
AC7: Given Contacts include the two seeded example contacts, when Muse calls contacts_lookup with a name that matches nobody, then The tool returns 'No contact found.'..
AC8: Given The Google routes are served, when The client requests Gmail search, then POST /api/google/mail/search is handled by the Google module..

document.objective: Lets a user connect Gmail, Google Calendar and a contacts list, decide what Muse may change in each, and give Muse tools to read and act on them.
document.summary: Gmail and Calendar connect together with one Google sign-in. Muse can read from a connected service at any time. Changes, such as creating an event, show an approval card unless the user set that connector to allow them, and sending an email always asks. Contacts live in the app, start with two examples, and the user can add or remove them.
userStories: As a user, I want to connect my Google account so that Muse can read my Gmail and Calendar instead of guessing.
As a user, I want to see what access I am granting before I continue so that I can consent knowingly.
As a user, I want Muse to ask before it changes my calendar or contacts, and always before it sends email, so that I stay in control.
As a user, I want to disconnect Google so that Muse's Gmail and Calendar tools are removed.
As a user, I want to manage a contacts list so that Muse can look up an email address before sending mail.

Google Calendar tools: calendar_list, calendar_add, calendar_remove
Contacts tools: contacts_lookup, contacts_add, plus manual add/remove on the page
Connection status shown as a nav badge and a pill
outOfScope: Web search and open-page tools (api/web), which are a separate web-browsing feature
Chrome extension browser bridge internals (chrome-extension/), which I did not read
Real Google Contacts sync; Contacts are local sample or user-entered data
Google OAuth server implementation details (server/google.js was not read)
Packaging or publishing the extension
functionalRequirements: The Connectors page shows one card per connector in the order Gmail, Google Calendar, Contacts, with a Connected or Not connected pill and the list of tools, marking write tools differently from read tools.
Clicking Connect on a Google connector shows a consent panel listing its scopes; Continue with Google navigates to /api/google/authorize and Cancel dismisses the panel.
On boot and after the OAuth redirect, the app queries Google status and sets Gmail and Calendar on or off together.
Disconnect Google calls the disconnect endpoint, turns off Gmail and Calendar, and records an audit entry.
Gmail permission is locked to Ask me first and the Allow button is disabled.
Calendar and Contacts write tools prompt for approval when the permission is Ask me first, and run without a prompt when it is Allow.
mail_send always shows an approval card with To, Subject and body and sends only if the user approves.
contacts_lookup matches contacts by name or email and returns a 'No contact found.' message on no match.
The nav badge shows the number of connected connectors.

risks: Contacts are stored in client state only. Whether state persists across devices or browsers is unconfirmed.
Gmail and Calendar share one OAuth grant, so the user cannot connect only one of them.
The Disconnect action ignores errors from the server (try/catch with an empty catch). The UI can show Disconnected even if the server-side revocation failed.
No tests or QA evidence tied to Connectors were seen. The features are shipped but not verified.
Only the local Express server's routes were read. The Vercel route consolidation was not checked for parity.
Gmail read and send scopes are sensitive and may trigger Google OAuth app verification.
openQuestions: Does the Contacts connector need real Google Contacts sync, or are local contacts intended?
Should users be able to connect Gmail and Calendar independently?
Do api/web and chrome-extension belong to the Connectors feature, or should they be specified as web-browsing and browser-bridge features?
What does server/google.js do for token refresh and scope errors?
limitations: I did not read server/google.js, core/api.js, core/registry.js, or the Chrome extension code, so OAuth, token handling, and bridge behavior are not described.
I did not run the app or tests, so no behavior has been verified.
I did not read api/web/search.js or server/web.js. I read api/web/open.js, which only forwards to handleOpen.
I did not read the Vercel api/google handlers.
document.howItWorks: The Connectors page (features/connectors) sends the browser to /api/google/authorize; the server keeps the tokens in an HttpOnly cookie. initConnectors reads /api/google/status at boot and after the redirect and switches both Google connectors together. The server's /api/google/* routes cover status, authorize, callback, disconnect, mail and calendar. Each connector adds its tools to the agent; write tools go through the approval flow.

features.name: Observability
features.summary: Records agent turns as traces in Postgres and shows them as a span waterfall with prompts, tokens and tool calls.

acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Given OBS_ENABLED is off, when a batch is posted, then nothing is written and the reply says disabled.
AC2: Given a signed-in user posts traces, when the server ingests them, then each trace carries the server's user id, not the browser's.
AC3: Given a post has no traces, spans or logs, when the server ingests it, then it returns 400.
AC4: Given content capture is off, when a prompt is recorded, then only its length is stored.
AC5: Given a captured string is longer than the cap, when it is stored, then it is cut to 10,000 characters with a truncated marker.
AC6: Given a trace is open, when its spans load, then the header says whether any tool ran.
AC7: Given no traces exist yet, when the page loads, then it says to send a chat message and refresh.
AC8: Given an unknown trace id is requested, when the server reads it, then it returns 404.

document.objective: Lets the builder replay any agent turn: what the model was sent, what it answered, which tools ran and how long each step took, to catch problems such as Muse claiming work it didn't do.
document.summary: The Observability page lists the 50 latest traces. Opening one shows a timeline of its steps, whether any tool ran, and the prompts, replies and tool inputs and outputs. Tracing can be turned off, or set to keep only the size of prompts and replies rather than their text. Captured text is cut at 10,000 characters.
userStories: As the builder, I want to see what the model was sent and what tools ran in a turn, so that I can debug wrong answers.
outOfScope: The user-facing activity log (How Muse works)

The system stores only a length when content capture is off.
The system caps captured text at 10,000 characters.
The system says whether a trace ran any tools.

document.howItWorks: The browser tracer (core/trace.js) and the server send spans and logs to /api/trace (api/trace.js → server/trace.js dispatch), stored in Postgres (Neon) by server/trace-store.js. OBS_ENABLED, OBS_CAPTURE_CONTENT, OBS_SAMPLE_RATE and OBS_RETENTION_DAYS control it; capContent in server/trace-core.js applies the 10,000-character cap. The page (features/observability) draws the waterfall from the spans.
